name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,711

clue.text: Originally widespread greeting in ancient Rome, and now in many other places?

definitions.text: Originally widespread greeting in ancient Rome, and now in many other places?

indicators.note: what comes originally comes at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
Ave was the Latin word of greeting, as in 'Ave Caesar'

explanation.surface: A gesture of greeting that began with the Romans and has spread across the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: W plus the Latin AVE gives WAVE, and a wave is how people greet each other almost everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising and moving a hand is a common gesture of hello in many countries, so it is a widespread greeting.

clue.text: Continue embracing rampant medic or large 25

indicators.note: a rampant beast rears up on its hind legs, and in a down entry rearing up means reading upwards
to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: 'go on' means continue
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: Someone urges a raging doctor to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is SETTER, the dog. The Gordon setter is the heaviest of the setter breeds, hence 'large'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gordon setter is a big black-and-tan Scottish gundog breed, one type of setter.

clue.text: Bottomless 14 flower

indicators.note: with no bottom, the final letter of a down entry is removed

blocks.note: the answer to 14 down

explanation.surface: A flower from Ireland without its base.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 down is IRISH; in a down entry the bottom is the last letter, so the H goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a garden plant with showy blooms, named for the Greek rainbow goddess.

clue.text: Leader held back by infrastructure

indicators.note: something held is kept inside, so the letters sit within the following word
going back means running the other way, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: four consecutive letters inside this word

explanation.surface: A head of state is propped up by roads and power lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Read inside infRASTructure backwards to find TSAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia, so a supreme ruler or head of state.

clue.text: Somehow, Peter is Dan Walker

indicators.note: done somehow means done in some unspecified way, so the letters can come in any order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Peter is somehow a man called Dan Walker, like a mistaken identity.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan Walker looks like a full name (he is a British TV presenter); the capital W hides the definition, a walker.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestrian is a person going on foot rather than in a vehicle.

clue.text: Starts to stockpile tequila and gin for pre-match party

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are used

blocks.note: opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Laying in spirits ahead of a party before the big day.
explanation.walkthrough: The match here is a marriage, not a football game: a stag party comes before a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag do is the groom's celebration with male friends before his wedding, which 'match' cheekily stands for.

clue.text: Exciting tale in which Romeo becomes dead chuffed

indicators.note: when one thing becomes another, a letter is exchanged for a different one

blocks.note: a gripping story full of suspense
R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: A gripping story in which Shakespeare's Romeo dies, leaving the reader happy.
explanation.walkthrough: The final R of THRILLER is swapped for D. 'Romeo' and 'dead' suggest Shakespeare's tragedy, but they are just letters. Chuffed is British slang for pleased.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone very pleased and delighted; chuffed is the informal British version.

clue.text: High society resting on fashionable result

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece resting on another sits above it

blocks.note: up means high
S is the abbreviation for society
something hot is in fashion

explanation.surface: The upper classes rely on following trends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High society' looks like one phrase meaning the elite, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An upshot is the final outcome or consequence of something.

clue.text: Early signs of aristocratic meltdown over unsuitable royal affair

indicators.note: the earliest sign of a word is its opening letter, so only those are used

blocks.note: opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A palace scandal: the first hints of an aristocrat's breakdown over an ill-judged royal romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word; everything before it supplies initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is a French loanword for a love affair, often a secret or illicit one.

clue.text: Where workers sew pants with pathos when exploited?

definitions.text: Where workers sew pants with pathos when exploited?

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, and rubbishy letters are ones to be rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A sad picture of exploited workers stitching trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like the garment being sewn, but here it is the British slang for rubbish, signalling a rearrangement of the letters around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatshop is a factory where people, often stitching clothes, work long hours for poor pay in bad conditions.

clue.text: Gamer? Send us error screens!

indicators.note: a screen conceals what is behind it, so the letters lie concealed in the words before

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning these three words

explanation.surface: A frustrated player demanding to see the error messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screens' looks like a noun for computer displays, but it is a verb meaning hides. The question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamer is one example of a person who finally operates a product, the consumer at the end of the chain.

clue.text: Kind of 25 nurse is hot, embracing good student

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one group of letters wraps around another

blocks.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
G is the abbreviation for good
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates
taken as written
H for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A feverish nurse hugging a promising pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: L for student comes from the learner plates on British cars. 25 is SETTER, here the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The English setter is a breed of gundog, so it is one variety of setter.

clue.text: Egyptian region is in a mess

indicators.note: something in a mess is jumbled and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A part of Egypt is in turmoil, like a news headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a mess' reads as a phrase, but 'in a' belongs to the letters and 'mess' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sinai peninsula, between the Gulf of Suez and the Gulf of Aqaba, is part of Egypt.

clue.text: You and me heading up north for our evening 25

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: you and I together are us
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A couple heading north together for an evening out.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is SETTER: here something that sets. Each evening the sun goes down, so it is our evening setter.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun sinks below the horizon every evening, so it is the thing that sets at dusk for us.

clue.text: Initiation of inalienable right is hard kind of 25

indicators.note: an initiation is a beginning, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written
H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Establishing an inalienable right is a hard job.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is SETTER, the dog breed; the red setter is properly called the Irish setter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish setter, with its glossy red coat, is a well-known breed of gundog and one variety of setter.

clue.text: Damp and occasionally downhearted

indicators.note: something done occasionally happens at intervals, so letters are picked at regular steps

blocks.note: every third letter of this word

explanation.surface: Feeling soggy and a bit low, like a rainy day.
explanation.walkthrough: Take every third letter: doWnhEarTed. 'Downhearted' looks like a second definition, but it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Damp and wet both describe something covered or soaked with water, so they are close synonyms.

clue.text: We lack Paul's awful and alarming indicator

indicators.note: something awful is in a terrible state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
taken letter for letter
the name only; the possessive ending supplies nothing

explanation.surface: A group lamenting that they are missing Paul's terrible something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alarming' has a double life: alarming as worrying, and as being like an alarm clock that rouses a sleeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A wake-up call is a warning that jolts people into noticing a problem, literally a call rousing a hotel guest.

clue.text: Distribute wholesale books

blocks.note: wholesale means everything, all of it
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A bulk supplier shipping out books to the trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wholesale books' reads as a trade instruction, but wholesale is the adjective meaning total and books is the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or assign portions to people, which is what distributing means.

clue.text: This 25, or a new 25

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
25 is SETTER, and hair gel sets a hairstyle

explanation.surface: The compiler calls themself a setter, or perhaps a brand-new one.
explanation.walkthrough: Angel is the pseudonym of this puzzle's compiler, so 'this setter' is a self-reference. In the wordplay the same 25 means a product that sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword compilers are called setters, and Angel is the pen name of the one who compiled this puzzle.

clue.text: Agree, lacking depth

blocks.note: lacking something means having no such thing
D is the abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: Going along with something without thinking it through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking' looks like a deletion signal, but here it supplies NO, followed by D.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding the head is the gesture of assent, so to nod is to agree or approve.

clue.text: Abuse could be a bit dire

indicators.note: 'could be' says the letters might become something else, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Mistreatment might be described as rather dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Abuse here is the noun meaning insulting language, not mistreatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter, forceful verbal attack, which is abuse in the sense of insults hurled at someone.

clue.text: Glimmering product of cuttlefish and cod

blocks.note: cuttlefish squirt dark ink
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A shimmering seafood dish of cuttlefish and cod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glimmering' reads as shiny, but here it is the noun: a glimmering of an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A glimmering is a faint first hint of understanding, the same as a slight suspicion or vague notion.

clue.text: Party against government, 25 for one

indicators.note: against means up close beside, so one piece sits right next to another

blocks.note: a do is a party
G is the abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: An opposition party taking on the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party against government' sounds political, but against just means next to. 'For one' marks 25 as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a gundog breed, so a setter is one example of the animal kept as a pet or hunting companion.

clue.text: Steady chap

blocks.note: first meaning: to secure with a rope, as a tent is held by its ropes
second meaning: an informal word for a man

explanation.walkthrough: 'Steady chap' looks like a description of a reliable man; it is two separate meanings, the first a verb from guy ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to secure with a rope that stays a mast or tent; as a noun it is a fellow.

clue.text: Fruit and vegetable champion

blocks.note: a pea is a vegetable
CH is the abbreviation for champion

explanation.surface: A prize-winning grower of fruit and vegetables at a village show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit and vegetable' reads as one phrase, but the fruit is the definition and the vegetable is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A peach is a soft, fuzzy-skinned stone fruit grown in warm climates.

clue.text: Muscle can 25

blocks.note: pec is short for pectoral, the chest muscle
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder boasting that brawn can do anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is SETTER, here a substance that makes things set. 'Can' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Pectin is the natural gelling agent in fruit that thickens jam, so it is something that makes preserves set.

clue.text: From this, tea and coffee run freely

definitions.text: From this, tea and coffee run freely

indicators.note: letters set free are no longer bound to their order, so they can be rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Hot drinks flowing from a big container at a church hall or office.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer, and inside it the word 'run', rearranged, gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a large metal container with a tap from which hot water, tea or coffee is dispensed.

clue.text: Passionate, if out of practice, when switching hands

indicators.note: to switch is to exchange one thing for another, so a letter is replaced

blocks.note: skills that are rusty have not been used lately
the right hand R becomes the left hand L

explanation.surface: An ardent lover, a little out of practice, changing hands.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L are the standard abbreviations for right and left, so changing hands swaps R for L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusty means full of vigour and sexual desire, which matches passionate in the sense of ardent and eager.

clue.text: Winding street leads to many found here

indicators.note: a winding course twists and turns, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A twisting road that brings lots of people to this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the puzzle itself: many of its answers are kinds of setter, such as dogs, gels and the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: This grid is full of answers defined as types of setter, so lots of setters really are found here.

clue.text: China has Tory elements ejected from corrupt meritocracy

indicators.note: what is ejected is thrown out, so some letters are removed
something corrupt is debased and twisted, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
the letters of this word, scattered through the longer one, are taken out

explanation.surface: The country of China sees Conservatives thrown out of a crooked system of merit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is porcelain. Removing T, O, R and Y from the long word leaves MEICRAC to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: China is fine porcelain, and porcelain is a kind of ceramic, so ceramic describes china.

clue.text: Doctor working a 25 in the morning, maybe

blocks.note: MO is a medical officer
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A doctor doing an early shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is SETTER, here something that goes down below the horizon, as the moon often does around dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon can sink below the horizon early in the day, so it may be something that sets at dawn.

clue.text: Be accepted around the French 25

indicators.note: to go around something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: to get in is to be admitted
la is the French feminine for 'the'

explanation.surface: Gaining entry around a French person.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is SETTER, here a substance that makes liquids set.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatin is the protein that makes jellies and desserts firm, so it is a classic setting agent.

clue.text: Turn over penny fine

blocks.note: a go is a turn in a game
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
D was the symbol for a penny in old British money

explanation.surface: Hand over a penny as a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn over' looks like a reversal instruction, but each word is its own piece. 'Fine' looks like a penalty; it means good.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine and good are synonyms for something satisfactory or of acceptable quality.

clue.text: Chance absence if the first of 26 becomes the 21st

indicators.note: when one thing becomes another, a letter is exchanged for a different one

blocks.note: a lack is an absence
the first of the alphabet's 26 letters, the one taken out
the 21st letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A gamble on someone being missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is not the clue at 26 across: it is the 26 letters of the alphabet, whose first is A. Swap A for U in LACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Chance and luck both name the unplanned force that decides whether things go well or badly.

clue.text: Picked up elements of resonant scent

indicators.note: elements are component parts, so the letters come from part of the next word
in a down entry, picking up means lifting from bottom to top

blocks.note: four consecutive letters inside this word

explanation.surface: Catching parts of a strong, lingering smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts as a homophone signal, and 'knows' does sound right, but the letters are in rESONant, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's nose is its aroma or bouquet, so nose can mean the scent of something.

clue.text: This writer's untidy biro log reveals a confused situation

indicators.note: untidy things are in disorder, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: this writer is the setter, and 'this writer's' is I'm, I am
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: The setter's messy handwritten notes show a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer's' is the setter speaking: this writer is = I'M. A biro is a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is an Italian loanword for a complicated, embarrassing mess or entanglement.

clue.text: Musical game

blocks.note: first meaning: a stage musical by the ABBA songwriters and Tim Rice
second meaning: the board game of kings and pawns

explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical game' reads like musical chairs; it is two separate meanings, a show and a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1984 stage show by Benny Andersson, Björn Ulvaeus and Tim Rice shares its title with the board game played on sixty-four squares.
